body.text: Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s> (Proof of Momentary Destruction).

body.text: namaḥ samantabhadrāya /
body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Samantabhadra</s>!

body.text: ākṣiptavyatirekā ya vyāptiranvayarūpiṇī /
body.translated_text: The <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) which has the form of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), with the negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) implied,

body.text: sādharmmyavati dṛṣṭānte sattvahetorihocyate //
body.translated_text: is here stated [as established] in the example possessing similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), for the reason of existence (<s>sattva</s>).

body.text: yat sat tat kṣaṇikaṃ yathā ghaṭaḥ santaścāmī vivādāspadībhūtāḥ padārthā iti /
body.translated_text: Whatever exists is momentary, like a pot; and these disputed objects exist — thus [is the inference].

body.text: hetoḥ parokṣārthapratipādakatvaṃ hetvābhāsatvaśaṅkānirākaraṇamantareṇa na śakyate pratipādayituṃ / hetvābhāsāśca asidvavirudvānaikāntikabhedena trividhāḥ / tatra na tāvadayamasidvo hetuḥ / yadi nāma darśane darśane nānāprakāraṃ sattvalakṣaṇamuktamāste, arthakriyākāritvaṃ, sattāsamavāyaḥ, svarūpasattvaṃ, utpādavyayaghrauvyayogitvaṃ pramāṇaviṣayatvaṃ, sadupalambhapramāṇagocaratvaṃ vyapadeśaviṣayatvamityādi, tathāpi kimanena aprastutena idānīmeva niṣṭaṅkitena / yadeva hi pramāṇato nirūpyamāṇaṃ padārthānāṃ sattvamupapannaṃ bhaviṣyati; tadeva vayamapi svīkariṣyāmaḥ / kevalaṃ yadetadarthakriyākāritvaṃ sarvvajanaprasidvamāste; tat khalvatra sattvaśabdenābhisandhāya sādhanatvenopāttaṃ / tacca yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣānumānapramāṇaprasidvasadbhāveṣu bhāveṣu pakṣīkṛteṣu pratyakṣādinā pramāṇena pratītamiti na svarūpeṇāśrayadvāreṇa vāsidvasambhāvanāpi //
body.translated_text: The capacity of the reason (<s>hetu</s>) to establish an imperceptible object cannot be demonstrated without removing the suspicion of its being a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>). And pseudo-reasons are of three kinds, distinguished as: unestablished (<s>asiddha</s>), contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), and inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). Therein, first, this reason is not unestablished. Even though in various philosophical systems the definition of existence (<s>sattvalakṣaṇa</s>) has been stated in various ways — causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), inherence in universal being (<s>sattāsamavāya</s>), existence as own nature (<s>svarūpasattva</s>), possessing origination, decay, and permanence (<s>utpāda-vyaya-dhrauvy-yogitva</s>), being the object of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇaviṣayatva</s>), being within the range of the means of apprehending the existent (<s>sadupalambhapramāṇagocaratva</s>), being the object of verbal designation (<s>vyapadeśaviṣayatva</s>), and so forth — nevertheless, what use is this irrelevant [discussion], inscribed just now? For whatever existence of objects, when examined by valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>), will be established — that alone we too shall accept. Only this causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyākāritva</s>), which is universally acknowledged, is here intended by the word 'existence' and taken up as the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>). And that [causal efficacy], being cognized by a valid means of knowledge such as perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) in entities whose existence is established through perception and inference (<s>anumāna</s>), and which have been made the thesis-subject (<s>pakṣa</s>) — therefore there is not even the possibility of it being unestablished, whether in its own nature or through the substratum (<s>āśraya</s>).

body.text: nāpi viruddhaḥ / sapakṣīkṛte ghaṭe sadbhāvāt / nanu kathamasya sapakṣatvaṃ, pakṣavadatrāpi kṣaṇabhaṅgāsiddheḥ / nahyasya pratyakṣata kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ / tathātvenāniścayāt / nāpi sattvānumānataḥ / punarnidarśanāntarāpekṣāyāmanavasthāprasaṅgāt / na cānyadanumānamasti /
body.translated_text: Nor is it contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because of its presence in the pot, which has been made the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>). [Objection:] But how is this a positive example? Because momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) is unestablished here too, just as in the thesis-subject. For the proof of its momentary destruction is not through direct perception, due to uncertainty as such. Nor through inference from existence — because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>) if another example were required. Nor is there another inference [available].

body.text: sambhave vā tenaiva pakṣe 'pi kṣaṇabhaṅgasidveralaṃ sattānumāneneti cet / ucyate / anumānāntarameva prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyyayātmakaṃ ghaṭe kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhakaṃ pramāṇāntaramasti, tathā ghaṭo varttamānakṣaṇe tāvat ekāmarthakriyāṃ karoti / atītānāgatakṣaṇayorapi kiṃ tāme vārthakriyāṃ kuryādanyāṃ vā, navā kāmapi kriyāmiti trayaḥ pakṣāḥ / nātra prathamapakṣo yuktaḥ kṛtasya karaṇāyogāt / atha dvitīyo 'bhyupagamyate tadidamatra vicāryyatām / yadā ghaṭo varttamānakṣaṇabhāvi kāryyaṃ karoti tadā kimatītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvinyapi kāryye śakto 'śakto vā / yadi śaktastadā varttamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryyavat atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvyapi kāryyaṃ kuryyāt tatrāpi śaktatvāt śaktasya kṣepāyogāt / anyathā varttamānakṣaṇabhāvino 'pi kāryyasyākaraṇaprasaṅgāt pūrvvāparakālayorapi śaktatvenāviśeṣāt, samarthasya ca sahakāryyapekṣāyā ayogāt / athāśaktastadā ekatra kāryye śaktāśaktatvaviruddhadharmmādhyāsāt kṣaṇavidhvaṃso ghaṭasya durvvāraprasaraḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: [Objection continued:] Or, if [momentariness] is possible [to prove by that inference], then even in the thesis-subject, the inference from existence suffices for proving momentary destruction — so what need is there for the inference [from the example]? [Reply:] We say: There is indeed another inference — a separate means of knowledge, consisting of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> (reversal of the reductio) — that establishes momentary destruction in the pot. Thus: the pot, in the present moment at least, performs one causal function (<s>arthakriyā</s>). With respect to past and future moments also, does it perform that very same causal function, or a different one, or no function at all? — these are the three alternatives. The first alternative is not tenable here, because of the impossibility of doing what has already been done. Now, if the second is accepted, then let this be examined: when the pot performs the effect belonging to the present moment, is it then capable or incapable with respect to effects belonging to past and future moments? If capable, then it should produce effects belonging to past and future moments just as [it produces] the present moment's effect, since it is capable there too, and because delay is impossible for what is capable. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of not producing even the present moment's effect, because there is no difference in capability between earlier and later times, and because something fully capable cannot depend on auxiliary causes. If incapable, then due to the superimposition of contradictory properties — capability and incapability — upon one [entity] with respect to [its] effects, momentary destruction of the pot would be an irresistible consequence.

body.text: nāpi tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ saṅgacchate śaktasvabhāvānuvṛttereva / yadā hi śaktasya svabhāvasya vilambo 'pyasahyastadā dūrītsāritamakaraṇam / anyathā vārttamānikasyāpi kāryyasyākaraṇaṃ syāt ityuktaṃ / tasmād yad yadā yajjananavyavahārapātraṃ, tattadā tat kuryyāt / akurvvacca na jananavyavahārabhājanam / tadevamekatra kāryye samarthetarasvabhāvatayā pratikṣaṇaṃ bhedāt ghaṭasya sapakṣatvamakṣatam /
body.translated_text: Nor does the third alternative hold, precisely because of the persistence of the capable nature. For when even delay is intolerable for a nature that is capable, then non-performance is [all the more] eliminated. Otherwise, as stated, there would be non-performance even of the present moment's effect. Therefore, whatever is the receptacle of the activity of producing whatever at whatever time, that produces that at that time. And [something] that does not produce is not a receptacle of productive activity. Thus, since the pot has a nature that is capable with respect to one effect and different [with respect to another], and because of moment-by-moment difference, the status of the pot as a positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>) remains unimpaired.

body.text:
atra prayogaḥ / yad yadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tattadā tajjanayatyeva / yathā antyā kāraṇasāmagrī svakāryyaṃ / atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryyajananavyavahārayogyaścāyaṃ ghaṭo varttamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryyakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle 'pīti svabhāvahetuprasaṅgaḥ / asya ca dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryyakaraṇavyavahāragocaratvasya prasaṅgasādhanasya vārttamānikakāryyakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle ca ghaṭe dharmmiṇi parābhyupagamamātrataḥ sidvatvāt asidvistāvadasambhavinī / nāpi virudvatā, sapakṣe antyakāraṇasāmagryāṃ sadbhāvasambhavāt /
nanvayaṃ sādhāraṇānaikāntiko hetuḥ / sākṣādajanake 'pi kuśūlādyavasthitavījādau vipakṣe samarthavyavahāragocaratvasya sādhanasya darśanāditi cet / na / dvividho hi samarthavyavahāraḥ pāramārthikaḥ aupacārikaśca / tatra yatpāramārthikam jananaprayuktaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ tadiha sādhanatvenopāttaṃ / tasya ca kuśūlādyavasthita vījādau kāraṇakāraṇatvāt aupacārikajananavyavahāraviṣayabhūte sambhavābhāvāt kutaḥ sādhāraṇānaikāntikatā / na cāsya sandigdhavyatirekitā viparyyaye bādhakapramāṇasadbhāvāt / tathāhīdaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ niyataviṣayatvena vyāptamiti sarvvajanānubhavasiddham / na cedaṃ nirnimittaṃ / deśakālasvabhāvaniyamābhāvaprasaṅgāt / na ca jananādanyannimittamupalabhyate / tadanvayavyatirekānuvidhānadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: Here is the formal argument (<s>prayoga</s>): Whatever is fit for the conventional usage of producing something at a given time, that necessarily produces it at that time — just as the final aggregate of causal conditions [produces] its own effect. And this pot, which is fit for the conventional usage of producing effects belonging to past and future moments, [should do so] even at the time of producing its present-moment effect, even at the time of the completion of all activity — this is the undesirable consequence from the essential nature of the reason (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>). And since this undesirable consequence — namely, the argument (<s>sādhana</s>) that [the pot] falls within the scope of the conventional usage of producing effects belonging to the second and subsequent moments — is established merely by the opponent's own admission with respect to the pot as the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) at the time of producing the present effect and at the time of the completion of all activity, the [fallacy of] unestablishedness does not even arise. Nor is there contradiction, because the presence [of the reason] in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>), the final aggregate of causal conditions, is possible. Now, if it is objected: 'This reason is inconclusive due to being common (<s>sādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), because the argument — being within the scope of the conventional usage of capability — is seen in the negative example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) as well, namely in seeds stored in a granary and the like, which do not directly produce [their effects]' — [we reply:] No. For the conventional usage of capability is of two kinds: ultimate (<s>pāramārthika</s>) and figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>). Among these, what is taken here as the reason to be proved is the ultimate fitness for the conventional usage of production, which is connected with [actual] production. And since the seed stored in a granary, being merely a cause of a cause, is the object only of figurative conventional usage of production, and since there is no possibility [of the ultimate usage] in it — whence comes the inconclusiveness of being common? Nor does this [reason] have doubtful non-deviation (<s>sandigdhavyatirekitā</s>), because there exists a means of proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>) that invalidates [the non-deviation] in the opposite case. For it is established through everyone's experience that this fitness for the conventional usage of production is pervaded by having a fixed object (<s>niyataviṣayatva</s>). And this [fixity] is not without a cause — because there would be the absurd consequence of no restriction in place, time, or nature. Nor is any cause for it apprehended other than [actual] production — because [the fixity] is observed to follow the presence and absence of [actual] production.

body.text: yadi ca jananamantareṇāpi jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ syāt tadā sarvvasya sarvvatra jananavyavahāra ityaniyamaḥ syāt / niyataścāyaṃ pratītaḥ / tato jananābhāve vipakṣe niyataviṣayatvasya vyāpakasya nivṛttau nivarttamānaṃ jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ janana eva viśrāmyatīti vyāptisidveranavadyo hetuḥ / na caiṣa ghaṭo varttamānakāryyakaraṇakṣaṇe sakalakriyātikramaṇe ca atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryyaṃ janayati / tato na jananavyavahārayogyaḥ / sarvvaḥ prasaṅgaḥ prasaṅgaviparyyayaniṣṭha iti nyāyāt /
body.translated_text: And if the fitness for the conventional usage of production were to exist even without [actual] production, then there would be no restriction — the conventional usage of production of everything everywhere [would follow]. But this [restriction] is apprehended as fixed. Therefore, since in the negative example (<s>vipakṣa</s>) — namely, the absence of production — the fitness for the conventional usage of production ceases along with the cessation of its pervader, namely fixed objecthood, it rests in production alone. Thus the reason is faultless due to the establishment of pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>). And this pot does not produce effects belonging to past and future moments at the time of producing its present-moment effect or at the time of the completion of all activity. Therefore it is not fit for the conventional usage of production [of those effects]. Every undesirable consequence culminates in the reverse of the undesirable consequence — such is the principle.

body.text: atrāpi prayogaḥ / yadyadā yanna karoti / tattadā tatra samarthavyavahārayogyaṃ yathā śālyaṅkuramakurvvan kodravaḥ śālyaṅkure / na karoti caiṣa ghaṭo varttamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryyakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle cātītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryyamiti vyāpakānupalabdhirbhinatti samarthakṣaṇādasamarthakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Here too is a formal argument: Whatever does not produce something at a given time is not fit for the conventional usage of capability with respect to that at that time — just as <s>kodrava</s> (a type of grain), not producing a rice-sprout, [is not fit for the conventional usage of capability] with respect to a rice-sprout. And this pot does not produce effects belonging to past and future moments at the time of producing the present-moment effect or at the time of the completion of all activity. Thus, the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) separates the incapable moment from the capable moment.

body.text: atrāpyasiddhirnāsti varttamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryyakaraṇakāle sakalakriyātikramakāle ca atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryyakaraṇasyāyogāt / nāpi virodhaḥ sapakṣe bhāvāt / na cānaikāntikatā pūrvvoktena nyāyena samartha vyavahāragocaratvajanakatvayovidhibhūtayoḥ sarvvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt /
body.translated_text: Here too there is no unestablishedness, because the production of effects belonging to past and future moments is impossible at the time of producing the present-moment effect and at the time of the completion of all activity. Nor is there contradiction, because [the reason] is present in the positive example (<s>sapakṣa</s>). Nor is there inconclusiveness, because — by the reasoning stated above — pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), which encompasses all instances, is established between the two positive entities: being within the scope of the conventional usage of capability and being a producer.

body.text: yatpunaratroktaṃ yadyadā yanna karoti na tattadā tatra samarthamityatra kaḥ karotyarthaḥ / kiṃ kāraṇatvaṃ? tatkāryyotpādānuguṇasahakārisākalyaṃ? āhosvit kāryyāvyabhicāraḥ? kāryyasambandho veti? tatra kāraṇatvameva karotyarthaḥ / tataḥ pakṣāntarabhāvino doṣā anabhyupagamapratihatāḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, as to what is said here: 'In the statement "whatever does not produce something at a given time is not fit for the conventional usage of capability with respect to that at that time" — what is the meaning of "produces"? Is it causality? Or the completeness of cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārisākalya</s>) favorable to the production of its effect? Or the invariable concomitance with the effect? Or the connection with the effect?' — among these, the meaning of 'produces' is just causality itself. Therefore, the defects belonging to the other alternatives are warded off by non-acceptance.

body.text: na cātrapakṣe kāraṇatvasāmarthyayoḥ paryyāyatvena vyāpakānupalambhasya sādhyāviśiṣṭatvamabhidhātumucitaṃ / samarthavyavahāragocaratvābhāvasya sādhyatvāt / kāraṇatvasamarthavyavahāragocaratvayośca bṛkṣaśiṃśapayoriva vyāvṛttibhedo 'stītyanavasara eva evaṃvidhasya kṣudrapralāpasya / tadevaṃ prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyyayahetudvayabalato ghaṭe dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ siddhaḥ / tatkathaṃ sattvādanyadanumānaṃ dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgasādhakam / nāstītyucyate / na caivaṃ sattvahetorvaiyarthyaṃ / dṛṣṭāntamātra eva prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyyayābhyāṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgaprasādhanāt nanvābhyāmeva pakṣe 'pi kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhirastviti cet / astu ko doṣaḥ / yo hi pratipattā prativastu yadyadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tattadā tajjanayatītyā dikamupanyasituṃ analasastasya tata eva kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhiḥ / yastu prativastu tannyāyopanyāsaprayāsabhīruḥ sa ttvekatradharmmiṇi yadyadā yajjananavyavahārayogyaṃ tattadā tajjanayatītyādinyāyena sattvamātramasthairyyavyāptamavadhāryyasattvādevānyatra kṣaṇikatvamavagacchatīti / kathamapramattovaiyarthyamasyācakṣīta tadevamekārthakāriṇo ghaṭasya dvitīyādikṣaṇabhāvikāryyāpekṣayā samarthetarasvabhāvavirudvadharmmā dhyāsāt bheda eveti kṣaṇabhaṅgatayā sapakṣatāmāvahati ghaṭe sattveheturupalabhyamāno na virudvaḥ /
body.translated_text: And in this case, it is not proper to state that the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) is not different from the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum), on the grounds that causality (<s>kāraṇatva</s>) and capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) are synonymous. For the absence of being an object of the conventional practice of capacity is itself what is to be proven. And since there is a distinction through exclusion between causality and being an object of the conventional practice of capacity — just as between a tree and a <s>śiṃśapā</s> (Dalbergia) — there is no occasion at all for such petty prattle. Thus, by the force of the two reasons — <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyyaya</s> (reverse of the reductio) — momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) is established in the example of the pot. Then how can it be said that there is no inference other than existence (<s>sattva</s>) that proves momentariness in the example? It cannot be said thus. And in this way, there is no futility of the reason of existence, since momentariness is established in the example alone through <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyyaya</s>. If one objects: 'Let momentariness be established in the thesis (<s>pakṣa</s>) as well through these two alone' — let it be so; what fault is there? For the one who is able to present the argument that 'whatever is capable of producing the conventional practice of generation at a given time regarding a given object, that thing generates that effect at that time, and so forth' — for that person, momentariness is established from that very reasoning. But one who is timid about the effort of presenting that reasoning for each individual property-bearer — that person, having ascertained through the reasoning 'whatever is capable of producing the conventional practice of generation at a given time, that generates the effect at that time, and so forth' regarding a single property-bearer, that mere existence is pervaded by impermanence, understands momentariness elsewhere from existence alone. How then could an attentive person declare its futility? Thus, the pot, which accomplishes a single purpose, having a nature that is capable with respect to the effect belonging to the second and subsequent moments, possesses a contradictory property through superimposition (<s>adhyāsa</s>) — it is indeed different [at each moment], and being momentary thus establishes positive concomitance (<s>sapakṣatā</s>). The reason of existence, being observed in the pot, is not contradicted.

body.text: na cāya manaikāntikaḥ / atraiva sādharmmyavati dṛṣṭānte sarvvopasaṃhāravatyā vyāpteḥ prasādhanāt / nanu viparyyaye bādhakapramāṇabalābdyāptisiddhistasya copanyāsavārttāpi nāsti tatkathaṃ vyāptiḥ prasādhiteti cet / tadetat taralatarabuddhivilasitaṃ / tathā hi uktametat varttamānakṣaṇabhāvikāryyakaraṇakāle atītānāgatakṣaṇabhāvikāryye 'pi ghaṭasya śaktisambhave tadānīmevaitat karaṇamakaraṇe ca śaktāśaktasvabhāvatayā pratikṣaṇaṃ bheda iti kṣaṇikatvena vyāptaiva sā arthakriyāśaktiḥ /
body.translated_text: And this reason is not inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), since <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) is established in this very homologous example (<s>sādharmyavat dṛṣṭānta</s>) through a comprehensive induction (<s>sarvopasaṃhāra</s>). [Objection:] 'But the establishment of the reverse [pervasion] is obtained through the force of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), and there is not even any question of presenting that — so how is the <s>vyāpti</s> established?' This is a display of an extremely fickle intellect. For it has been stated: at the time of producing the effect belonging to the present moment, if the pot also has the capacity for the effect belonging to past and future moments, then it would produce that effect at that very time; and since it would and would not [produce simultaneously], being of the nature of capable and incapable, there is difference at every moment — thus, that <s>arthakriyāśakti</s> (capacity for causal efficacy) is indeed pervaded by momentariness.

body.text: nanvevaṃ anvayamātramastu vipakṣāt punarekāntena vyāvṛttiriti kuto labhyamiti cet, vyāptisiddhereva / byatirekasandehe vyāptisiddhireva kathamiti cet, na dvividhā hi vyāptisiddhiranvayarūpā ca karttṛdharmmaḥ / sādhanadharmmavati dharmmiṇi sādhyadharmmasyāvaśyambhāvo yaḥ / vyatirekarūpā ca karmmadharmmaḥ sādhyābhāve sādhanasyāvaśyamabhāvo yaḥ / enayoścaikatarapratītiniyamena dvitīyapratītimākṣipati / anyathā, ekasyāḥ eva siddhaḥ / tasmād / yathā viparyyaye bādhakapramāṇabalāt niyamavati vyatireke siddhe anvayaviṣayaḥ saṃśayaḥ pūrvvaṃ sthito 'pi paścātparigalati / tato 'nvayaprasādhanārthaṃ na pṛthaksādhanamucyate / tathā prasaṅgatadviparyyayahetudvayabalato niyamavatyanvaye siddhe vyatirekaviṣaye pūrvvaṃ sthito 'pi sandehaḥ paścātparigalatyeva / na ca vyatirekasādhakamanyat pramāṇaṃ vyaktavyam / tataśca sādhyābhāve sādhanasyaikāntiko vyatirekaḥ / sādhane sati sādhyasyāvaśyamanvayo veti na kaścidarthabhedaḥ tadevaṃ viparyyayabādhakapramāṇamantareṇāpi prasaṅgaprasaṅgaviparyyayahetudvayabalāt anvayarūpavyāptisidvau sattvahetoranaikāntikasyābhāvādataḥ sādhanāt kṣaṇabhaṅgasidviranavadyeti /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'Even so, let there be mere positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>); but from where is the definite exclusion from the dissimilar cases (<s>vipakṣa</s>) obtained?' — From the very establishment of <s>vyāpti</s>. [Objection:] 'How can <s>vyāpti</s> be established when there is doubt about negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)?' — The establishment of <s>vyāpti</s> is not twofold: the form of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), which is the agent-property — the necessary presence of the <s>sādhyadharma</s> (property to be proven) in the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) possessing the <s>sādhanadharma</s> (proving property); and the form of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), which is the object-property — the necessary absence of the <s>sādhana</s> (proving property) in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s> (property to be proven). By the ascertainment of either one of these, the second is also drawn in. Otherwise, the establishment of just one would be sufficient. Therefore, just as when negative concomitance with a fixed relation is established through the force of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> in the reverse case, any doubt previously existing regarding the domain of positive concomitance subsequently vanishes — and thus no separate proof need be stated for establishing positive concomitance — even so, when positive concomitance with a fixed relation is established through the force of the two reasons of <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyyaya</s>, any doubt previously existing regarding the domain of negative concomitance subsequently vanishes as well. Nor need another <s>pramāṇa</s> proving negative concomitance be stated. Therefore, the definite negative concomitance of the <s>sādhana</s> in the absence of the <s>sādhya</s>, and the necessary positive concomitance of the <s>sādhya</s> when the <s>sādhana</s> is present — there is no difference in meaning between these. Thus, even without a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> for the reverse case, since through the force of the two reasons of <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyyaya</s> the <s>vyāpti</s> in the form of positive concomitance is established, and since the reason of existence is free from inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — therefore, the establishment of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) through this proof is faultless.

body.text: nanu ca sādhanamidamasidvaṃ, na hi kāraṇabudhyā kāryyaṃ gṛhyate / tasya bhāvitvāt / na ca kāryyabudhyā kāraṇam / tasyātītatvāt / na ca varttamānagrāhiṇā jñānena atītānāgatayorgrahaṇamatiprasaṅgāt / na ca pūrvvāparayoḥ kālayorekaḥ pratisandhātāsti kṣaṇabhaṅgabhaṅgaprasaṅgāt / kāraṇābhāve tu kāryyābhāvapratītiḥ svasambedanavādino manorathasyāpyaviṣayaḥ / na ca pūrbbotarakālayoḥ sambittī tābhyāṃ vāsanā tayā ca hetuphalāvasāyī vikalpa iti yuktaṃ / sa hi vikalpo gṛhītānusandhāyako 'tadrūpasamāropako vā na prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ / ekasya pratisandhāturabhāve pūrvvāparagrahaṇayorayogāt / vikalpavāsanāyā evābhāvāt / nāpi dvitīyaḥ; marīcikāyāmapi jalavijñānaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgāt / tadevamanvayavyatirekayorapratipatterarthakriyālakṣaṇam sattvamasidvamiti //

kiñca prakārāntarādapīdaṃ sādhanamasidvaṃ / tathā hi vījādīnāṃ sāmarthyaṃ vījādijñānāt kāryyādaṅkurādervā niścetavyaṃ / kāryyatvañca vastutvasidvau sidhyati, vastutvañca kāryyāntarāt / kāryyāntarasyāpi kāryyatvaṃ vastutvasidvau / tadvastutvañca tadaparakāryyāntarādityanavasthā / athānavasthābhayāt paryyante kāryyāntaraṃ nāpekṣate, tadā tenaiva pūrvveṣāmasattvaprasaṅgāt naikasyāpyarthakriyāsāmarthyaṃ sidhyati / nanu kāryyatvasattvayorbhinnavyāvṛttikatvāt / sattāsidvāvapi kāryyatvasidvau kā kṣatiriti cet / tadasaṅgatam, satyapi kāryyatvasattvayorvyāvṛttibhede sattvasidvau kutaḥ kāryyatvasiddhiḥ / kāryyatvaṃ hyabhūtvābhāvitvaṃ, bhavanañca sattā / sattā ca saugatānāṃ sāmarthyameva / tataśca sāmarthyasandehe bhavatītyeva vaktumaśakyaṃ kathamabhūtvābhāvitvaṃ kāryyatvaṃ setsyati / apekṣitaparavyāpāratvaṃ kāryyatvamityapi nāsato dharmmaḥ sattvañca sāmarthyaṃ tacca sandigdhamiti kutaḥ kāryyasiddhiḥ / tadasidvau pūrvvasya sāmarthyaṃ na sidhyatīti sandigdhāsidvo hetuḥ /

tathā virudvo 'pyayaṃ, tathā hi kṣaṇikatve sati na tāvat ajātasyānanvayanirudvasya vā kāryyārambhakatvaṃ sambhavati / na ca nispannasya tāvān kṣaṇo 'sti yamupādāya kasmaicit kāryyāya vyāpāryyet / ataḥ kṣaṇikapakṣa eva arthakriyānupapattervirūdvatā / athavā vikalpena yadupanīyate, tatsarvvamavastu, tataśca vastvātmake kṣaṇikatve sādhye 'vastūpasthāpayannanumānavikalpo virudvaḥ / yadvā, sarvvasyaiva hetoḥ kṣaṇikatve sādhye virudvatvaṃ deśakālāntarānanugame sādhyasādhanabhāvābhāvāt anugame ca nānākālamekamakṣaṇikaṃ kṣaṇikatvena virudhyata iti /
anaikāntiko 'pyayaṃ sattvasthairyyayorvirodhābhāvāditi / pratrocyate /
yattāvaduktaṃ sāmarthyaṃ na pratīyata iti / tat kiṃ sarvvathaiva na pratīyate / kṣaṇabhaṅgapakṣe vā /

prathamapakṣe sakalakārakajñāpakahetucakrocchedāt mukhaspandanamātrasyāpyakaraṇaprasaṅgaḥ / anyathā yenaiva vacanena sāmarthyaṃ nāstīti pratipādyate tasyaiva tat pratipādanasāmarthyamavyāhatamāyātam / tasmāt paramapuruṣārthasamīhayā vastutattvanirūpaṇapravṛttasya śaktisvīkārapūrvvakaiva pravṛttiḥ / tadasvīkāre tu na kaścit kvacit pravartteteti nirīhaṃ jagajjāyate / atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ / tadāsti tāvat sāmarthyapratītiḥ / sā ca kṣaṇikatve yadi nopapadyate tadā virudvaṃ vaktumucitaṃ, asidvamiti tu nyāyabhūṣaṇīyaḥ prāyovilāpaḥ / na ca satyapi kṣaṇikatve sāmarthyapratītivyāghātaḥ / tathāhi kāraṇajñānopādeyabhūtena kāryyagrāhiṇā jñānena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbheṇa asya bhāve asya bhāva iti anvayaniścayo janyate, tathā kāraṇāpekṣayā bhūtalakaivalyagrāhijñānopādeyabhūtena kāryyāpekṣayā bhūtalakaivalyagrāhiṇā jñānena tadarpitasaṃskāragarbhaṇa asyābhāve asyābhāva iti vyatirekaniścayo janyate / yadāhurguravaḥ /
body.translated_text: On the first alternative, since the entire wheel of reasons that indicate all agents would be destroyed, there would be the unwanted consequence of not performing even a mere movement of the mouth [i.e., speech itself would be impossible]. Otherwise, the very statement by which it is demonstrated that capability does not exist — that very statement's capability to demonstrate would come through unobstructed. Therefore, one who proceeds to determine the true nature of reality, aspiring to the highest human goal, proceeds only with the prior acceptance of capability. Without accepting it, nobody would engage in anything — the world would become inert. Now, the second alternative: then the cognition of capability does indeed exist. And if it is not tenable under momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>), then it is fitting to state a contradiction; but saying 'it is unestablished' is mostly just a lamentation worthy of the <s>Nyāyabhūṣaṇa</s>. And there is no conflict with the cognition of capability even when momentariness is accepted. For thus: the ascertainment of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) — 'when this is present, that is present' — is generated by a cognition grasping the effect, which is the object adopted by the cognition of the cause, together with the latent impression (<s>saṃskāra</s>) deposited by it. Likewise, the ascertainment of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>) — 'when this is absent, that is absent' — is generated by a cognition grasping the mere ground [without the effect], adopted with reference to the cause, by means of a cognition grasping the mere ground [without the cause], adopted with reference to the effect, together with the latent impression deposited by it. As the teachers say:

children.translated_text: A second cognition arising immediately after one determinate awareness gives rise to the reflection of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>).
Likewise, another cognition born from the experience of the absence of that same [cause] produces the understanding of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>).

body.text: evaṃ sati gṛhītānusandhāyake evāyaṃ vikalpaḥ / upādānopādeyabhūtakramipratyakṣadvayagṛhītānusandhānāt / yadāhālaṅkāraḥ /
body.translated_text: This being so, this conceptual cognition operates only upon what has been grasped and followed up — because it follows up what is grasped by two perceptions (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) that are successive, serving as substrate (<s>upādāna</s>) and supervenient (<s>upādeya</s>). As the <s>Alaṅkāra</s> says:

body.text: yadi nāmaikamadhyakṣaṃ na pūrvvāparavittimat /
body.translated_text: 'Even if a single perception does not have earlier and later cognition,

body.text: adhyakṣadvayasadbhāve prākparāvedanaṃ kathamiti /
body.translated_text: since two perceptions exist, how [is there no] earlier and later awareness?'

body.text:
nāpi dvitīyo 'sidvaprabhedaḥ / sāmarthyaṃ hi sattvamiti saugatānāṃ sthitireṣā / na caitat prasādhanārthamasmākamidānīmeva prārambhaḥ; kintu yatra pramāṇapratīte vījādau vastubhūte dharmmiṇi pramāṇapratītaṃ sāmarthya tatra kṣaṇābhaṅga sādhanāya / tataścāṅkurādīnāṃ kāryyādaśanāt āhatyasāmarthyasandehe 'pi paṭupratyakṣaprasidvaṃ sanmātratvamavadhāryyameva / anyathā na kvacidapi vastumātrasyāpi pratipattiḥ syāt / tasmācchāstrīyasattvalakṣaṇasandehe 'pi paṭupratyakṣavalāvalambitavastubhāve aṅkurādau kāryyatvamupalabhyamānaṃ vījādeḥ sāmarthyamupasthāpayatīti nāsidvidoṣāvakāśaḥ /
nāpi kśaṇikatve sāmarthyakṣatiḥ, yato virudvatā syāt, kṣaṇikatvaniyataprāgbhāvitvalakṣaṇakāraṇatvayovirodhābhāvāt, kṣaṇamātrasthāyinyapi sāmarthyasambhavāditi nādimo virodhaḥ / nāpi dvitīyo virodhaprabhedaḥ / avastuno vastuno vā svākārasya grāhyatve 'pi, adhyavaseyavastvapekṣayaiva sarvvatra prāmāṇyapratipādanāt vastusvabhāvasyaiva kṣaṇikatvasidviriti kva virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor is the second type of unestablishedness [viable]. For 'capability is existence (<s>sattva</s>)' — this is the established position of the Buddhists (<s>saugatas</s>). And this is not an undertaking begun by us now for the first time in order to prove it; rather, wherever capability is cognized through a means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) in a real subject (<s>dharmin</s>) such as a seed, there [it is used] for proving momentariness. Therefore, even if there is doubt about the aggregate capability due to the non-observation of effects such as sprouts and the like, mere existence (<s>sanmātratva</s>) — well-established by keen perception (<s>paṭupratyakṣa</s>) — must be ascertained. Otherwise, there would be no cognition of even a mere thing anywhere. Therefore, even if there is doubt about the definition of existence (<s>sattvalakṣaṇa</s>) in the treatises, the effecthood (<s>kāryatva</s>) observed in sprouts and the like — whose thingness rests upon keen perception — establishes the capability of seeds and the like. So there is no room for the defect of unestablishedness. Nor is capability harmed under momentariness, since that would imply contradiction — because there is no conflict between the causality characterized by being that which was invariably antecedent, which is determined by momentariness, [and capability]; and because capability is possible even for what endures for only a moment — thus there is no first type of contradiction. Nor is there the second type of contradiction. For even though the own-form (<s>svākāra</s>) of a non-real or real [thing] is grasped, since the validity of knowledge is demonstrated everywhere only with reference to the determined real object (<s>adhyavaseyavastu</s>), the establishment of momentariness belongs to the very own-nature of things — so where is the contradiction?

body.text: yacca gṛhyate yaccādhyavasīyate te dve api anyanivṛttī na vastunī svalakṣaṇāvagāhitve abhilāpasaṃsargānupapatteriti cet / na / adhyavasāyasvarūpāparijñānāt agṛhīte 'pi vastuni mānasyādipravṛttikārakatvaṃ vikalpasyādhyavasāyitvaṃ, apratibhāse 'pi pravṛttiviṣayīkṛtatvamadhyavaseyatvam / etaccādhyavaseyatvaṃ svalakṣaṇasyaiva yujyate, nānyasya / arthakriyārthitvāt arthipravṛtteḥ / evañcādhyavasāye svalakṣaṇasyāsphuraṇameva / na ca tasyāsphuraṇe 'pi sarvvatrāviśeṣeṇa pravṛttyākṣepaprasaṅgaḥ, pratiniyatasāmagrīprasūtāt, pratiniyatasvākārāt, pratiniyataśaktiyogāt, pratiniyata evātadrūpaparāvṛtte apratīte 'pi pravṛttisāmarthyadarśanāt / yathā sarvvasyāsattve 'pi vījādaṅkurasyaivotpattiḥ dṛṣṭasya niyatahetuphalabhāvasya pratikṣeptumaśakyatvāt / paraṃ vāhyenārthena sati pratibandhe prāmāṇyamanyathātvaprāmāṇyamiti viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: If it is objected: 'Both what is grasped [by perception] and what is ascertained [by conceptual cognition] are exclusions from what is other (<s>anyāpoha</s>), not real entities, since the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) cannot be connected with verbal expression' — [we reply:] No. Due to non-comprehension of the nature of ascertainment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>): even without the real entity being grasped, conceptual cognition's being the cause of practical engagement, such as [the engagement of] a mind [directed toward action], is its character as ascertainment; and even without [the entity] appearing, the fact that it is made the object of practical engagement is what it means to be ascertained. And this character of being ascertained pertains only to the particular (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), not to anything else — because practical engagement is directed toward causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>). And thus, in ascertainment, the particular itself does not manifest. Yet even when it does not manifest, there is no absurd consequence of undiscriminating practical engagement in everything, because [the cognition] is produced from a fixed aggregate of conditions, has a fixed own-form, possesses a fixed capacity, and — even without the exclusion from what is other (<s>atadrūpaparāvṛtti</s>) being itself cognized — the power of practical engagement toward that fixed [object] is observed. Just as, even though everything is non-existent [at the time of production], only the sprout arises from the seed, because the observed fixed cause-effect relationship cannot be rejected. Furthermore, the distinction [is this]: when there is a real connection with the external object, there is validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>); otherwise, invalidity.

body.text: tathā tṛtīyo 'pi pakṣaḥ prayāsaphalaḥ / nānākālasyaikasya vastuno vastuto 'sambhavepyatadrūpaparāvṛttayoreva sādhyasādhanayoḥ pratyakṣeṇa vyāptigrahaṇāt / dvividho hi pratyakṣasya viṣayo grāhyo 'dhyavaseyaśca sakalātadrūpaparāvṛttaṃ vastumātraṃ sākṣādasphuraṇāt pratyakṣasya grāhyo viṣayo mā bhūt / tadekadeśagrahaṇe tu tanmātrayorvyāptiniścāyakavikalpajananādadhyavaseyo viṣayo bhavatyeva / kṣaṇagrahaṇe santānaniścayavat / rūpamātragrahaṇe ghaṭaniścayavacca / anyathā sarvvānumānocchedaprasaṅgāt / tathā hi vyāptigrahaḥ sāmānyayoḥ, viśeṣayoḥ, sāmānyaviśiṣṭaviśeṣayo rviśeṣaviśiṣṭasāmānyayorveti vikalpāḥ / nādyo vikalpaḥ sāmānyasya vādhyatvāt / avādhyatve 'pyadṛśyatvāt / dṛśyatve 'pi puruṣārthānupayogitayā tasyānumeyatvāyogāt / nāpyanumitāt sāmānyāt viśeṣānumānam, sāmānyasarvvaviśeṣayorvakṣyamāṇanyāyena pratibandhapratipatterayogāt / nāpi dvitīyo viśeṣasyānanugāmitvāt / antime tu vikalpadvaye sāmānyādhāratayā dṛṣṭa eva viśeṣaḥ sāmānyasya viśeṣyo viśeṣaṇaṃ vā karttavyaḥ / adṛṣṭa eva vā deśakālāntaravarttī / yadvā dṛṣṭādṛṣṭātmako deśakālāntarabartī atadrūpaparāvṛttaḥ sarvvo viśeṣaḥ / na prathamaḥ pakṣo 'nanugāmittvāt; nāpi dvitīyaḥ, adṛṣṭatvāt / na ca tṛtīyaḥ, prastutaikaviśeṣadarśane 'pi deśakālāntaravarttināmadarśanāt /
body.translated_text: Likewise, the third alternative too is fruitless in its endeavor. For even though a single entity existing at different times is impossible in reality, pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) between the two — the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) — both being mere exclusions from what is other (<s>atadrūpaparāvṛtti</s>), is grasped through perception. For perception has two kinds of objects: what is grasped and what is ascertained. The mere entity, [taken as] the complete exclusion from what is other, may not be the directly grasped object of perception, since it does not directly manifest in its entirety. But in the grasping of a part of it, since [that grasping] generates a conceptual cognition that determines the pervasion of those two mere [exclusions], it does become the ascertained object. Just as in the grasping of a momentary [instance], a determination of the continuum [arises]; and just as in the grasping of mere form, a determination of a pot [arises]. Otherwise, there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all inference. For the alternatives regarding the grasping of pervasion are: [it is] between two universals, between two particulars, between a universal-qualified particular and a particular-qualified universal. The first alternative is not [correct], because the universal is invalidated [as a real entity]. Even if not invalidated, because it is imperceptible. Even if perceptible, because it is of no use for human purposes and hence cannot be what is to be inferred. Nor can a particular be inferred from an inferred universal, because — by the reasoning to be stated — it is impossible to ascertain the connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) between a universal and all [its] particulars. Nor [is valid] the second alternative, because the particular does not persist [across instances]. But in the last two alternatives, the particular, seen as the basis of the universal, must be made either the qualificand or the qualifier of the universal. Or else it is simply unseen, existing at other places and times. Or the particular, existing at other places and times, consisting of both seen and unseen, [constituting] the complete exclusion from what is other. The first [sub-]option is not [correct], because [the particular] does not persist. Nor the second, because [the other-place-and-time particulars are] unseen. Nor the third, because even when one particular of the type under discussion is seen, those existing at other places and times are not seen.

body.text: atha teṣāṃ sarvveṣāmeva viśeṣāṇāṃ sadṛśatvāt / sadṛśasāmagrīprasūtatvāt sadṛśakāryyakāritvāditi prattyāsattyā, ekaviśeṣagrāhakaṃ pratyakṣamatadrūpaparāvṛttamātreniścayaṃ janayadatadrūpaparāvṛttaviśeṣamātrasya vyavasthāpakam / yathaikasāmagrīpratibadvarūpamātragrāhakaṃ pratyakṣaṃ ghaṭe niścayaṃ janayadghaṭagrāhakaṃ byavasthāpyate / anyathā ghaṭo 'pi ghaṭasantāno 'pi pratyakṣato na sidhyet sarvvātmanā grahaṇābhāvāt / tadekadeśagrahaṇantvatadrūpaparāvṛtte 'pyaviśiṣṭam / yadyevamanenaiva krameṇa sarvvasya viśeṣasya viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvavat vyāptipratipattirapyastu / tat kimarthaṃ nānākālamekakṣaṇikamabhyupagantavyaṃ yena kṣaṇikatve sādhanasya virudvatvaṃ syāt iti na kaścidvirodhaprabhedaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now, [if it is said:] because all those particulars are similar — because they are produced from similar aggregates of conditions, and because they produce similar effects — by this proximity (<s>pratyāsatti</s>), perception that grasps one particular, by generating a determination of mere exclusion from what is other, establishes [the pervasion for] all particulars that are merely exclusions from what is other. Just as perception that grasps mere form, bound to one aggregate of conditions, by generating a determination regarding a pot, is established as grasping the pot [as a whole]. Otherwise, neither the pot nor the pot-continuum could be established through perception, because there is no grasping of [the pot] in its entirety. And the grasping of a part of it is no different [in principle] even in [the case of] exclusion from what is other. If this is so, then by this very procedure, let the apprehension of pervasion regarding every particular [proceed], just like the qualifier-qualificand relation. In that case, why must a single [entity existing at] different times be accepted as momentary, such that the means of proof for momentariness would be contradictory? Thus, there is no absurd consequence of any variety of contradiction.

body.text: na cāyamanekāntiko 'pi hetuḥ / pūrvvoktakrameṇa sādharmmyadṛṣṭānte prasaṅgaviparyyayahetubhyāmanvayarūpavyāpteḥ prasādhanāt / nanu yadi prasaṅgaviparyyayahetudvayavalato ghaṭe dṛṣṭānte kṣaṇabhaṅgaḥ sidhyettadā sattvasya niyamena kṣaṇikatvena vyāptisidveranaikāntikatvaṃ na syāditi yuktam / kevala midamevāsambhavi / tathāhi śakto 'pi ghaṭaḥ kramisahakāryyapekṣayā kramikāryyaṃ kariṣyati /
body.translated_text: Nor is this reason inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) either, because <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) in the form of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is established in the homologous example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>) through the two reasons of <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> (reversal of the reductio), by the method previously stated. [Objection:] If momentary destruction is established in the example of the pot through the force of the two reasons of <s>prasaṅga</s> and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s>, then it is reasonable that there would be no inconclusiveness, since the pervasion of existence with momentariness would necessarily be established. However, this very thing is impossible. For even a capable pot will produce successive effects in dependence upon successive cooperative conditions (<s>kramisahakārin</s>).

body.text: na caitad vaktavyaṃ samartho 'rthaḥ svarūpeṇa karoti / svarūpañca sarvvadāstītyanupakāriṇi sahakāriṇyapekṣā na yujyata iti, satyapi svarūpeṇa kārakatve sāmarthyābhāvātkathaṃ karoti, sahakārisākalyaṃ hi sāmarthyaṃ tadvaikalyañcāsāmarthyaṃ / na ca tayorāvirbhāvatirobhāvābhyāṃ tadvataḥ kācit kṣatiḥ / tasya tābhyāmanyatvāt / tasmādarthaḥ samartho 'pi syāt na ca karotīti sandigdhavyatirekaḥ prasaṅgahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor should it be said that 'a capable entity produces by its own nature, and since its own nature always exists, dependence upon a cooperative condition that contributes nothing [new] is not appropriate.' Even granting causality by own nature, how does it produce, given the absence of capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>)? For capacity is the completeness of cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārisākalya</s>), and the absence thereof is incapacity. Nor does the appearance and disappearance of those [cooperative conditions] cause any damage to that which possesses them, because that [entity] is different from those [conditions]. Therefore, an entity might be capable yet not produce — thus the <s>prasaṅga</s> reason has doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>).

body.text: atrocyate / bhavatu tāvat sahakārisākalyameva sāmarthyaṃ / tathāpi so 'pi tāvadbhāvaḥ svarūpeṇa kārakaḥ / tasya ca yādṛśaścaramakṣaṇe 'kṣepakriyādharmmā svabhāvaḥ tādṛśa eva cet prathamakṣaṇe tadā tadāpi prasahya kurbbāṇo brahmaṇāpyanivāryyaḥ / na ca so 'pyakṣepakriyādharmmā svabhāvaḥ sākalye sati jāto bhāvādbhinna evābhidhātuṃ śakyaḥ / bhāvasyākarttṛtvaprasaṅgāt / evaṃ yāvadyāvat dharmāntaraparikalpastāvattāvadudāsīno bhāvaḥ / tasmādyadrūpamādāya svarūpeṇāpi janayatītyucyate; tasya prāgapi bhāve kathamajaniḥ kadācit / akṣepakriyāpratyanīkasvabhāvasya prācyasya paścādanuvṛttau kathaṃ kadācidapi kāryyasambhavaḥ / nanu yadi sa evaikaḥ karttā syāt yuktametat / kintu sāmagrī janikā tataḥ sahakāryyantaravirahavelāyāṃ balīyaso 'pi na kāryyaprasava iti kimatra virudvaṃ / na hi bhāvaḥ svarūpeṇakarotīti svarūpeṇaiva karoti / sahakārisahitādeva tataḥ kāryyotpattidarśanāt / tasmādyāptivat kāryyakāraṇabhāvo 'pi, ekatrānyayogabyavacchedena anyatrāyogavyavacchedena nāvabodvavyaḥ, tathaiva laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ sampratipatteriti /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: Let it be granted that capacity is indeed the completeness of cooperative conditions. Even so, that entity too is a cause by its own nature. And if the nature of that [entity] — which in the final moment has the property of non-delayable action (<s>akṣepakriyādharma</s>) — is exactly the same in the first moment, then even at that [first moment], forcibly producing [its effect], it would be unstoppable even by <s>Brahmā</s>. Nor can the nature having the property of non-delayable action, which arises when completeness [of conditions] obtains, be described as entirely different from the entity — because there would be the absurd consequence that the entity is not an agent. Thus, to the extent that one imagines other properties [as the cause], to that extent the entity [itself] becomes disengaged. Therefore, taking that form by virtue of which [the entity] is said to produce even by its own nature — if that [form] existed previously as well, how could there ever have been non-production? If the earlier nature, which is the opposite of non-delayable action, were to persist afterward, how could there ever be the arising of an effect? [Objection:] 'If that [entity] alone were the single agent, this would be correct. But the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) is the producer. Therefore, at the time when other cooperative conditions are absent, even a powerful [entity] does not give rise to its effect — what is contradictory in this? For [the fact] that an entity produces by its own nature does not mean that it produces by its own nature alone, because the arising of the effect is observed only from [the entity] combined with cooperative conditions. Therefore, causality (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) too, like pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), should not be understood merely through the determination of co-presence in one case and the determination of co-absence in another — since that is indeed how worldly investigators understand [things].'

body.text: atrocyate / yadā militāḥ santaḥ kāryyaṃ kurvvate tadaikārthakaraṇalakṣaṇaṃ sahakāritvamepāmastu ko niṣedvā? militaireva tu tatkāryya karttavyamiti kuto labhyate? pūrvvāparayorekasvabhāvatvādbhāvasya / sarvvadā jananājananayoranyataraniyataprasaṅgasya durvvāratvāt / tasmāt sāmagrī janika naikaṃ janakamiti sthiravādināṃ manorathasyāpyaviṣayaḥ / dṛśyate tāvadevamiti cet / dṛśyatāṃ kintu pūrvvasthitādeva sāmagrīmadhyapraviṣṭādbhāvāt kāryotpattiranyasmādeva vā viśiṣṭādbhāvādutpannāditi vivādapadam / tatra prāgapi sambhave sarvvadaiva kāryyotpatti rna vā kadācidapīti virodhamasamādhāya cakṣuṣī nimīlya tata eva kāryyotpattidarśanāditi sādhyānuvādamātrapravṛttaḥ kṛpāmarhatīti / na ca pratyabhijñādibalādekatvasidviḥ tat pauruṣasya lūnapunarjātakeśanakhādāvapyupalambhato nirddalanāt, lakṣaṇabhedasya ca darśayitumaśakyatvāt / sthirasidvidūṣaṇe cāsmābhiḥ prapañcato nirastatvāt / tasmāt sākṣāt kāryyakāraṇabhāvāpekṣayā ubhayatrāpyanyayogavyavacchedaḥ / vyāptau tu sākṣātparamparayā kāraṇamātrāpekṣayā kāraṇe vyāpake 'yogavyavacchedaḥ / kāryye vyāpye 'nyayogavyavacchedaḥ / tathā tadatatsvabhāve vyāpake 'yogavyavacchedaḥ / tatsvabhāve ca vyāpye 'nyayogavyavacchedo vikalpāruḍharūpāpekṣayā vyāptau dvividhamavadhāraṃam / nanu yadi pūrvvāparakālayorekasvabhāvo bhāvaḥ sarvvadājanakatvenājanakatvena vā vyāpta upalabdhaḥ syāttadāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ saṅgacchate / na kṣaṇabhaṅgavādinā pūrvvāparakālayorekaḥ kaścidupalabdha iti cet / tadetadatigrāmyaṃ / tathāhi pūrvvāparakālayorekasvabhāvatve satītyasyāyamarthaḥ / parakālabhāvī janako yaḥ svabhāvo bhāvasya sa eva yadi pūrvvakālabhāvī / pūrvvakālabhāvī vā yo 'janakaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa eva yadi parakālabhāvī, tadopalabdhameva jananamajananambā syāt, tathā ca sati sidvayoreva svabhāvayorekatvārope sidvameva jananamajananambāsajyata iti /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: When [the causes] have come together and produce the effect, let this cooperative causality (<s>sahakāritva</s>), characterized by accomplishing a single purpose, be theirs — who can deny it? But from where is it established that only the combined [causes] must produce that effect? Because an entity has one and the same nature at earlier and later times, and because the absurd consequence of being invariably fixed in either production or non-production at all times is unavoidable. Therefore, [the claim that] 'the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) is the producer, not a single producer' is beyond even the aspirations of the permanentists (<s>sthiravādin</s>). [Objection:] 'But this is directly observed!' — Let it be observed; but the point of dispute is whether the arising of the effect is from the entity that has persisted from before and has entered into the aggregate, or from a distinct entity that has newly arisen. Therein, without resolving the contradiction — that if [the entity] is capable even before [the aggregate is complete], then the effect should arise at all times, or not at all — one who merely closes one's eyes and says 'the arising of the effect is observed from that very aggregate' is merely restating the thesis (<s>sādhya</s>) and deserves compassion. And the establishment of identity through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) and the like does not hold, for that is refuted since personal identity is observed even in hair and nails that have been cut and have regrown, and since the distinguishing characteristics cannot be shown [to be identical]. And this has been extensively refuted by us in the section disproving permanence (<s>sthirasiddhidūṣaṇa</s>). Therefore, with regard to the direct cause-effect relation, in both cases there is exclusion of other connections (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>). But with regard to <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), considering direct and indirect causality in general: in the pervader, which is the cause, there is exclusion of disconnection (<s>ayogavyavaccheda</s>); in the pervaded, which is the effect, there is exclusion of other connections (<s>anyayogavyavaccheda</s>). Likewise, in the pervader, which is of a nature different from that [of the effect], there is exclusion of disconnection; and in the pervaded, which is of that same nature, there is exclusion of other connections — with regard to <s>vyāpti</s> considered through the conceptually superimposed form (<s>vikalpāruḍharūpa</s>), there is a twofold determination. [Objection:] 'If an entity has one and the same nature at earlier and later times, and if it were found to be pervaded by either always-producing or always-not-producing, then this <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) would be applicable. But the momentariness-advocate does not apprehend any single entity at earlier and later times.' — This is extremely crude. For the meaning of 'if an entity has one and the same nature at earlier and later times' is this: if the nature belonging to the later time that is a producer is the very same nature belonging to the earlier time; or if the nature belonging to the earlier time that is a non-producer is the very same belonging to the later time — then production or non-production would indeed be invariably observed. And this being so, when identity is superimposed upon what are in fact two established natures, production or non-production necessarily follows.

body.text: nanu kāryyameva sahakāriṇamapekṣate / na tu kāryyotpattihetuḥ / yasmāt dvividhaṃ sāmarthya nijamāgantukañca sahakāryyantaraṃ tato 'kṣaṇikasyāpi kramavat sahakārinānātvādapi kramavat kāryyanānātvopapatteraśakyaṃ bhāvānāṃ pratikṣaṇamanyānyatvamupapādayitumiti cet / ucyate / bhavatu tāvannijāgantukabhedena dvividhaṃ sāmarthyaṃ / tathāpi yat prātisvikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ arthakriyādharmmakamavaśyamabhyupagantavyaṃ tat kiṃ prāgapi paścādeva veti vikalpya yaddūṣaṇamugdīritaṃ / tatra kimuktamaneneti na pratīmaḥ / yattu kāryyeṇaiva sahakāriṇo 'pekṣanta ityupatkṛtaṃ tadapi nirupayogaṃ / yadi hi kāryyameva svajanmani svatantraṃ syādyuktametat / kevalamevaṃ sati sahakārisākalyasāmarthyakalpanamaphalaṃ / svātantryādeva hi kāryyaṃ kādācitkaṃ bhaviṣyati / tathā ca sati santo hetavaḥ sarvvathāsamarthāḥ / asadetat kāryyaṃ svatantramiti viśuddhā budviḥ / atha kāryyasyaivāyamaparādho yadidaṃ samarthe kāraṇe satyapi kadācinnopapadyata iti cet / na tattarhi tat kāryyaṃ svātantryāt / yadbhāṣyaṃ /
body.translated_text: [Objection:] 'It is the effect itself that requires cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>) — not the cause of the effect's arising. For capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>) is of two kinds: intrinsic (<s>nija</s>) and adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>). Since a different cooperative factor [is needed each time], even for a non-momentary entity, sequential diversity of effects is possible due to the sequential diversity of cooperative conditions — therefore it is impossible to establish the moment-by-moment differentness of entities.' — We reply: Let capacity be of two kinds, distinguished as intrinsic and adventitious. Even so, the particular nature of each individual thing — its own-characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>), which is characterized by causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — must necessarily be accepted. Considering whether that [nature] existed before or only afterward, the refutation that was set forth — what in that has been answered by this [objection]? We do not understand. As for the contribution that 'the effect itself requires cooperative conditions' — that too is useless. For if the effect were independent in its own arising, this claim would be justified. But in that case, the supposition of the capacity of the totality of cooperative conditions would be pointless, since the effect, being independent, would arise occasionally [of its own accord]. And in that case, the existing causes would be utterly incapable in every way. 'This effect, being non-existent [as a cause], is independent' — this would be the pure conclusion. But if one says 'It is the fault of the effect itself that, even when the capable cause exists, it sometimes does not arise' — then that effect would not be the effect of that [cause], due to its independence. As the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) says:

children.translated_text: Even when the cause remains the same in all states, if there is non-production,
the effect would thus be independent — and it would not be its effect in such a case.

body.text: atha na tadbhāve bhavatīti tatkāryyamucyate, kintu tadabhāvena bhavatyeveti vyatirekaprādhānyāditi cet / na / yadi hi svayambhavan bhāvayedeva hetuḥ svakāryyaṃ tadā tadabhāvaprayukto 'syābhāva iti pratītiḥ syāt / no ced yathā kāraṇe satyapi kāryyasvātantryānna bhavati / tathā tadabhāve 'pi svātantryādeva na bhūtamiti śaṅkā kena nivāryyeta / yadbhāṣyaṃ /
body.translated_text: Now, if it is said: 'An effect is not called [an entity's] effect because it comes into being when that [cause] exists, but rather because it comes into being [precisely] through the absence of that [cause] — thus the predominance is of negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>)' — [we reply:] No. For if the cause, existing of itself, were to necessarily bring about its own effect, then the cognition 'its absence is occasioned by the absence of that [cause]' would hold. But if, even when the cause exists, the effect does not arise due to the effect's own independence — then who could ward off the suspicion that even in the absence of that [cause], it simply did not arise due to its own independence? As the commentary states:

children.translated_text: "If even when that [cause] exists there is no arising, how can there be non-arising in its absence?
That its non-existence is occasioned by the absence of that [cause] — whence [can this be established]?"

body.text: tasmād yathaiva tadbhāve niyamena na bhavati / tathaiva tadbhāve niyamena bhavedeva / abhavacca na tatkāraṇatāmātmanaḥ kṣamate / yaccoktaṃ, prathamakāryyotpādanakāle hṛttarakāryyotpādanasvabhāvaḥ / ataḥ prathamakāla evāśeṣāṇi kāryyāṇi kuryyāditi / tadidaṃ mātā me vandhyetyādivat svavacananirodhādayuktaṃ, yo hṛttarakāryyajananasvabhāvaḥ sa kathamādau kāryyaṃ kuryyāt / na tarhi tatkāryyakaraṇasvabhāvaḥ na hi nīlotpādanasvabhāvaḥ pītādikamapi karotīti /
body.translated_text: Therefore, just as in the presence of that [cause] it necessarily does not arise [i.e., the future effect at the wrong time], so too in the presence of that [cause] it necessarily does arise [i.e., the proper effect at the proper time]. And non-existence cannot claim causality for itself. And as for the objection: 'At the time of producing the first effect, it has the nature of producing the later effect as well; therefore it should produce all effects at the first moment itself' — this is untenable, like saying 'my mother is barren,' because it is self-refuting. For how could that whose nature is to produce a later effect produce an effect at the beginning? It is simply not of the nature of producing that [first] effect. For one whose nature is to produce blue does not produce yellow and the like.

body.text: atrocyate / sthirasvabhāvatve hi bhāvasya uttarakālamevedaṃ kāryyaṃ na pūrvvakālamiti kuta etat / tadabhāvācca kāraṇamapi uttarakāryyakaraṇasvabhāvamityapi kutaḥ / kiṃ kurmmaḥ uttarakālameva tasya janmeti cet; astu sthiratve tadanupapadyamānamasthiratāmādiśatu; sthiṣtvepyeṣa eva svabhāvastasya yaduttarakṣaṇa eva karotīti cet / utedānīṃ pramāṇapratyāśā / dhūmādagnirityatrāpi svabhāva evāsya yadidānīmatra niragnirapi dhūma iti vaktuṃ śakyatvāt / tasmāt pramāṇasidve svabhāvāvalambanaṃ, na tu svabhāvāvalambanena pramāṇavyālopaḥ / tasmād yadi kāraṇasyottarakāryyakārakatvamabhyupagamya kāryyasya prathamakṣaṇabhāvitvamāsajyate, syāt svavacanavirodhaḥ / yadā tu kāraṇasya sthiratve kāryyasyottarakālatvamevāsaṅgatam / ataḥ kāraṇasyāpyuttarakāryyajanakatvaṃ vastuto 'sambhavi tadā prasaṅgasādhanamidaṃ / jananavyavahāragocaratvaṃ hi jananena vyāptamiti prasādhitaṃ / uttarakāryyajananavyavahāragocaratvañca tvadabhyupagamāt prathamakāryyakaraṇakāla eva ghaṭe dharmmiṇi sidvaṃ / atastanmātrānubandhina uttarābhimatasya kāryyasya prathame kṣaṇe 'sambhavādeva prasaṅgaḥ kriyate / na hi nīlakārake 'pi pītakārakatvārope pītasambhavaprasaṅgaḥ svavacanavirodhonāma / tadevaṃ śaktaḥ sahakāryyanapekṣitatvāt jananena vyāptaḥ / ajanayaṃśca śaktāśaktatvavirudvadharmmādhyāsādbhinna eva / nanu bhavatu prasaṅgaviparyyayabalādekakāryyaṃ pratiśaktāśaktatvalakṣaṇavirudvadharmmādhyāsaḥ / tathāpi na tato medaḥ sidhyati; tathāhi bījamaṅkurādikaṃ kurvvad yadi yenaiva svabhāvenāṅkuraṃ karoti tenaiva kṣityādikantadākṣityādīnāmapyaṅkurasvābhāvyāpattiḥ / nānāsvabhāvatvena tu kārakatve svabhāvānāmanyonyābhāvāvyabhicāritvādekatra bhāvābhāvau parasparavirudvau syātāmityekamapi bījaṃ bhidyeta / evaṃ pradīpo 'pi tailakṣayavarttidāhādikaṃ; tathā pūrvvarūpamapyuttararūparasagandhādikamanekaiḥ svabhāvaiḥ parikaritaṃ karoti / teṣāñca svabhāvānāmanyonyābhāvāvyabhicārādvirudvānāṃ yoge pradīpādikaṃ bhidyeta / na ca bhidyate / tanna ! virudvadharmmādhyāso bhedakaḥ, tathā bījasyāṅkuraṃ prati kārakatvaṃ garddabhādikaṃ pratyakārakatvamiti kārakatvākārakatve api virudvau dharmau / na ca tadyoge 'pi bījabhedaḥ / tadevamekatra bīje pradīpe rūpe ca vipakṣe paridṛśyamānaḥ śaktāśaktatvādirvirudvadharmmādhyāso na ghaṭāderbhedaka iti /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: If the entity has a permanent nature, then from where does it follow that 'this effect belongs only to the later time and not to the earlier time'? And in the absence of that [reason], from where is it established that the cause too has the nature of producing only the later effect? [Objection:] 'What can we do? Its birth is only at the later time.' — Let it be so; since under permanence this is untenable, let it point to impermanence. [Objection:] 'Even while persisting, this is simply its nature — that it produces only at the later moment.' — Now there is hope for a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)! For even in the inference 'from smoke, fire,' one could say 'it is simply its nature that here there is smoke even without fire' — since that could be said. Therefore, reliance on own nature must be grounded in what is established by a <s>pramāṇa</s>; but the abrogation of a <s>pramāṇa</s> through reliance on own nature is not acceptable. Therefore, if one accepts that the cause produces the later effect and then the absurd consequence follows that the effect belongs to the first moment, there would be self-contradiction (<s>svavacanavirodha</s>). But when, under the permanence of the cause, the very belonging of the effect to the later time is itself inconsistent — and therefore the cause's production of the later effect is also impossible in reality — then this is the <s>prasaṅga</s> proof. For it has been established that being within the scope of the conventional usage of production is pervaded by actual production. And being within the scope of the conventional usage of producing the later effect is established — by your own admission — in the pot as the <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), at the very time of producing the first effect. Therefore, the <s>prasaṅga</s> is constructed precisely because of the impossibility, at the first moment, of the later intended effect that depends solely on that [permanent nature]. For in the case of attributing the capacity to produce yellow even to what produces blue, the absurd consequence of the arising of yellow is not a case of self-contradiction. Thus, what is capable, by not requiring cooperative conditions, is pervaded by actual production. And what does not produce, through the superimposition of the contradictory properties of capability and incapability (<s>śaktāśaktatva</s>), is indeed different [from its capable state]. [Objection:] 'Let there be, through the force of <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s>, the superimposition of contradictory properties characterized as capability and incapability with respect to a single effect. Even so, difference (<s>bheda</s>) is not thereby established. For a seed producing a sprout and so forth — if by the very nature by which it produces a sprout it also produces earth and so forth, then for earth and the like too, the absurd consequence of having the nature of a sprout would follow. But if production is by means of diverse natures, since those natures invariably do not coexist with each other, the presence and absence [of different natures] at one locus would be mutually contradictory — and thus even a single seed would be divided. Likewise the lamp too produces the consumption of oil, the burning of the wick, and so forth; and the earlier form too produces subsequent form, taste, smell, and so forth, each fashioned by multiple natures. And since those natures invariably do not coexist, when contradictory natures combine, the lamp and the like would be divided. But they are not divided. Therefore, the superimposition of contradictory properties is not a cause of division. Likewise, the seed's causality with respect to a sprout and its non-causality with respect to a donkey and the like — these causality and non-causality are also contradictory properties. But even with their conjunction, the seed is not divided. Thus, the superimposition of contradictory properties such as capability and incapability, being observed in the negative examples (<s>vipakṣa</s>) of a single seed, lamp, and form, does not cause the division of the pot and the like.'

body.text: atra brūmaḥ / bhavatu tāvadvījādīnāmanekakāryyakāritvādvarmmabhūtānekasvabhāvabhedastathāpi kaḥ prastāvovirudvadharmmādhyāsasya / svabhāvānāṃ hyanyonyābhāvāvyabhicāre bhedaḥ prāptāvasaro na virodhaḥ / virodhastu yadvidhāne yanniṣedho yanniṣedhe yadvidhānaṃ tayorekatradharmmiṇi parasparaparihārasthitatayā syāt / tadatraikaḥ svbhāvaḥ svābhāvena virudvo yukto bhāvābhāvavat / na tu svabhāvāntareṇa / ghaṭatvavastutvavat / evamaṅkurādikāritvaṃ tadakāritvena virudvaṃ na punarvastvantarakāritvena / pratyakṣavyāpāraścātra yathā nānādharmmairadhyāsitaṃ bhāvamabhinnaṃ vyavasthāpayati / tathā tatkāryyakāriṇaṃ kāryyāntarākāriṇañca / tadyadi pratiyogitvābhāvādanyonyābhāvāvyabhicāri ṇāvapi svabhāvāvavirudvo tatkārakatvānyākārakatve vā viṣayabhedādavirudve, tat kimāyātamekakāryyamprati śaktāśaktatvayoḥ parasparapratiyoginīrvirudvayordharmmayoḥ / etayorapi punaravirodhe virodho nāma dattajalāñjaliḥ / bhavatu tarhyekakāryyāpekṣayaiva sāmarthyāsāmarthyayorvirodhaḥ / kevalaṃ yathā tadeva kāryyaṃ prati kvaciddeśe śaktirdeśāntare cāśaktiriti deśabhedādavirudve śaktayaśaktī tathaikatraiva kāryye kālabhedādapyavirudve / yathāpūrvvaṃ nniḥkriyaḥ sphaṭikaḥ sa eva paścāt sakriya iti cet /
body.translated_text: To this we say: Let there indeed be a distinction of multiple natures, constituting [real] properties, in seeds and the like, due to their producing multiple effects. Even so, what occasion is there for the superimposition of contradictory properties? For when natures invariably entail the absence of each other, there is [just] difference, not contradiction. Contradiction, however, would exist when the affirmation of one entails the negation of the other and vice versa, such that the two, existing in one and the same subject (<s>dharmin</s>), abide in mutual exclusion. Thus, here one nature is properly contradicted by its own absence — just as existence and non-existence [contradict each other]. But not by a different nature — just as 'potness' and 'thingness' [do not contradict each other]. Likewise, producing a sprout and the like is contradicted by not producing that [sprout], but not by producing another entity. And the operation of perception here, just as it establishes as undivided an entity superimposed with various properties, so too [it establishes] it as producing that effect and as not producing another effect. Therefore, if the two natures — even though they invariably entail each other's absence — are not contradictory due to the absence of being counter-correlatives, or if producing that [effect] and producing another are not contradictory due to difference of object, then what has been gained regarding capability and incapability with respect to one effect, which are contradictory properties that are mutual counter-correlatives? And if even these two are not contradictory, then the very notion of contradiction is given away. Let it then be that the contradiction between capability and incapability is only with respect to one [particular] effect. But just as capability with respect to that very effect exists in one place and incapability in another — and the two are not contradictory due to difference of place — so too, with respect to one and the same effect, [they are] not contradictory due to difference of time. As [one might say]: 'Previously, this crystal was inactive; later, it became active.'

body.text: ucyate / na hi vayaṃ paribhāṣāmātrādekatra kāryye deśabhedādavirudve śaktyaśaktī brūmaḥ / kintu virodhābhāvāt / taddeśakāryya kāritvaṃ hi taddeśakāryyākāritvena virudvaṃ / na punardeśāntare tatkāryyākāritvenānyakāryyakāritvena vā / yadyevantatkālakāryyakāritvaṃ tatkālakāryyākāritvena virudvaṃ / na punaḥ kālāntare tatkāryyākāritvenānyakāryyakāritvena vā / tatkathaṃ kālabhede 'pi virodha iti cet / ucyate / dvayorhi dharmmayorekatradharmmiṇyanavasthitiniyamaḥ parasparaparihārasthitilakṣaṇo virodhaḥ / sa ca sākṣātparasparapratyanīkatayā bhāvābhāvavadvā bhavet / ekasya vā niyamena pramāṇāntareṇa bādhanānnityatvasattvavadvā bhavediti na kaścidarthabhedaḥ / tadatraikadharmmiṇi tat kālakāryyakāritvādhāre kālāntare tatkāryyākāritvasyānyakāryyakāritvasya vā niyamena pramāṇāntareṇa bādhanādvirodhaḥ / tathā hi yatraiva dharmmiṇi tatkālakāryyakāritvamupalabdhanna tatraiva kālāntare tat kāryyākāritvamanyakāryyakāritvaṃ vā brahmaṇāpyupasaṃharttuṃ śakyate, yenānayoravirodhaḥ syāt / kṣaṇāntare kathita prasaṅgaviparyyayahetubhyāmavaśyambhāvena dharmmibhedaprasādhanāt / na ca pratyabhijñānādekatvasidviḥ / tat pauruṣasya nirmmūlitatvāt / ata eva vajro 'pi pakṣakūkṣau nikṣiptaḥ kathamasau sphaṭiko varākaḥ kālabhedenābhedāsādhanāya dṛṣṭāntībhavitumarhati / na caivaṃ samānakālakāryyāṇāṃ deśabhede 'pi dharmmibhedo yukto bhedasādhakapramāṇābhāvādindriyapratyakṣeṇa nirastavibhramāśaṅkenābhedaprasādhanācca / iti na kālabhede 'pi śaktyaśaktyorvirodhaḥ svasamayamātrādapahastayituṃ śakyaḥ / samayapramāṇayorapravṛtteriti /
body.translated_text: [Reply:] It is said: We do not assert that capability and incapability are non-contradictory with respect to one effect due to difference of place merely on the basis of a stipulation — but rather because there is no contradiction [in that case]. For the production of that-place's effect is contradicted by the non-production of that-place's effect — but not by the non-production of that [same] effect in another place, or by the production of another effect. Likewise, the production of that-time's effect is contradicted by the non-production of that-time's effect — but not by the non-production of that [same] effect at another time, or by the production of another effect. 'Then how is there contradiction even in the difference of time?' — it is said: Contradiction is defined as the rule of non-co-existence of two properties in one and the same subject, characterized by their abiding in mutual exclusion. And this would be either directly, through being mutually opposed — like existence and non-existence — or through one being necessarily invalidated by another means of proof (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — like eternality and existence. There is no real difference [between these cases]. Here, in the very subject that supports the production of that-time's effect, the non-production of that [same] effect at another time, or the production of another effect, is necessarily invalidated by another means of proof — hence there is contradiction. For in the very subject where the production of that-time's effect is apprehended, the non-production of that effect at another time or the production of another effect cannot be established even by <s>Brahmā</s>, such that there would be no contradiction between these. Because the difference of the subject is necessarily established, in another moment, by the <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> (reversal) reasons already stated. Nor is the unity [of the subject] established through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), because that [recognition] has been uprooted as being merely conventional. For this very reason, the wretched crystal — even if pressed into the belly of the thesis — cannot serve as an example for establishing non-difference through temporal difference. Moreover, for effects at the same time, even in difference of place, the difference of the subject is not warranted — due to the absence of a means of proof that establishes difference, and because non-difference is established by sense-perception whose suspicion of error has been removed. Thus, the contradiction between capability and incapability even in temporal difference cannot be brushed aside merely on the basis of one's own convention — because conventions and valid means of proof do not [always] coincide.

body.text: tasmāt sarvvatra virudvadharmmādhyāsasidvireva bhedasidviḥ / vipratipannaṃ prati tu virudvadharmmādhyāsādbhedavyavahāraḥ sādhyate / nanu tathāpi sattvamidamanaikāntikamevāsādhāraṇatvāt sandigdhavyatirekatvādvā / yathā hīdaṃ kramākramanivṛtto akṣaṇikānnivṛttaṃ, tathā sāpekṣatvānāpekṣatvayorekatvānekatvayorapi vyāpakayornivṛttau kṣaṇikādapi / tathāhyupasapaṇapratyayena devadattakarapallavādinā sahacaro vījakṣaṇaḥ pūrvvasmādeva puñjāt samarthojāto 'napekṣa ādyātiśayasya janaka iṣyate / tatra ca samānakuśūlajanmasu bahuṣu vijasantāneṣu kasmāt kiñcideva vījaṃ paramparayāṅkurotpādānuguṇamupajanayati bījakṣaṇānnānye vījakṣaṇā bhinnasantānāntaḥpātinaḥ / nahyupasarpaṇapratyayāt prāgeva teṣāṃ samānāsamānasantānavarttināṃ vījakṣaṇānāṃ kaścit paramparātiśayaḥ / athopasarpaṇāt prāṅna tat santāna varttino 'pi janayanti paramparayāpyaṅkurotpādānuguṇaṃ vījakṣaṇaṃ vījamātrajananātteṣāṃ / kasyacideva vījakṣaṇasyopasarpaṇapratyayasahabhuva ādyātiśayotpādaḥ / hanta tarhi yadabhāve satyutpannopi na janayedeva / tathā kevalānāṃ vyabhicārasambhavādādyātiśayotpādamaṅkuraṃ vā prati kṣityādīnāṃ parasparāpekṣāṇāmevotpādakatvamakāmakenāpi svīkarttavyaṃ / ato na tāvadanapekṣā kṣaṇikasya sambhavinī / nāpya pekṣā yujyate / samasamayakṣaṇayoḥ savyetaragoviṣāṇayorivopakāryyopakārakabhāvāyogāditi nāsidvaḥ prathamo vyāpakābhāvaḥ / api cāntyo vījakṣaṇo 'napekṣo 'ṅkurādikaṃ kurvvan yadi yenaiva rūpeṇāṅkuraṃ karoti tenaiva kṣityādikaṃ / tadā kṣityādīnāmapi aṅkurasvābhāvyāpattirabhinnakāraṇātvāditi na tāvadekatvasambhavaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, everywhere, the establishment of difference is precisely through the establishment of the superimposition of contradictory properties (<s>viruddhadharmādhyāsa</s>). But for one who is in dispute, the convention of difference is proved from the superimposition of contradictory properties. [Objection:] Even so, this existence (<s>sattva</s>) [as a reason] is indeed inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), due to being uncommon (<s>asādhāraṇa</s>) or due to having doubtful exclusion (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>). For just as this [reason], being excluded from sequence (<s>krama</s>) and non-sequence (<s>akrama</s>), is excluded from the non-momentary, so too, upon the exclusion of the pervaders — dependence (<s>sāpekṣatva</s>) and independence (<s>anāpekṣatva</s>), oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) and multiplicity (<s>anekatva</s>) — [it would be excluded] from the momentary as well. For thus: a seed-moment (<s>bījakṣaṇa</s>), accompanied by the approaching auxiliary condition (<s>upasarpaṇapratyaya</s>) such as the hand-sprout of <s>Devadatta</s>, having arisen capable from the prior aggregate itself, is held to be independent, as the generator of the initial superiority (<s>ādyātiśaya</s>). And therein, among the many seed-continua born from the same granary, why does only a particular seed generate in succession [something] conducive to the production of a sprout? [Why] not other seed-moments falling within different continua? For prior to the approaching condition, there is no successive superiority among those seed-moments existing in the same or different continua. If, prior to the approach, even those existing in that continuum do not generate a seed-moment conducive to the successive production of a sprout — since they only generate a mere seed — then only for a particular seed-moment, co-existing with the approaching condition, is there the production of the initial superiority. Alas, then, even one that has arisen would not produce when that [approaching condition] is absent. Likewise, since deviation is possible for [the causes] taken singly, with respect to the production of the initial superiority or the sprout, the productiveness of earth and the like must be accepted as mutually dependent, even unwillingly. Therefore, independence of the momentary is not possible to begin with. Nor is dependence tenable — because the relation of benefited and benefiter between two simultaneous moments is impossible, like the left and right horns [of a cow] — thus the first absence of the pervader is not established. Moreover, if the final seed-moment, being independent, producing the sprout and so forth, produces earth and the like by that very form by which it produces the sprout, then there would be the absurd consequence that earth and the like also have the nature of sprouts, because the cause is non-different — thus oneness is not possible either.

body.text: nanu rūpāntareṇa karoti / tathā hi vījasyāṅkuraṃ pratyupādānatvaṃ kṣityādikaṃ tu prati sahakāritvaṃ / yadyevaṃ sahakāritvopādānatve kimekantatvaṃ nānā vā / ekañceta kathaṃ rūpāntareṇa janakaṃ / nānātve tvanayorvījādbhedo 'bhedo vā / bhede kathaṃ vījasya janakatvaṃ tābhyāmevāṅkurādīnāmutpatteḥ / abhede vā kathaṃ vījasya na nānātvaṃ bhinnatādātmyāt / etayorvā ekatvamekatādātmyāt / yadyucyeta / kśityādau janayitavye tadupādānam purvvameva kṣityādivījasya rūpāntaramiti / na tarhi vījantadanapekṣaṃ kṣityādīnāṃ janakaṃ / tadanapekṣatve teṣāmaṅkurodbhedānupapatteḥ / na cānupakārakāṇyapekṣanta iti tvayaivoktaṃ / na ca kṣaṇasyopakārasambhavo 'nyatra jananāt tasyābhedyatvādityanekatvamapi nāstīti dvitīyo 'pi vyāpakābhāvo na sidvaḥ / tasmādasādhāraṇānaikāntikatvaṃ gandhavattvavaditi / yadi manyetānupakārakā api bhavanti sahakāriṇo 'pekṣaṇīyāśca kāryyeṇānuvihitabhāvābhāvāt sahakaraṇācca / nanvanena krameṇākṣaṇikopi bhāvo 'nupakārakānapi sahakāriṇaḥ kramavataḥ kramavatkāryyeṇānukṛtānvayavyatirekānapekṣiṣyate / kariṣyate ca kramavat sahakārivaśaḥ krameṇa kāryyāṇīti vyāpakānupalabdherasidveḥ / sandigdhavyatirekamanaikāntikaṃ sattvaṃ kṣaṇikatvasidvāviti //
body.translated_text: [Objection:] But it produces by a different form. For thus: the seed has the status of material cause (<s>upādānatva</s>) with respect to the sprout, but the status of cooperative cause (<s>sahakāritva</s>) with respect to earth and the like. If so, are cooperative-cause-status and material-cause-status one or many? If one, how does it produce by a different form? If many, is there a difference or non-difference of these two from the seed? If different, how is the seed the producer — since the sprout and the like arise from those two [properties] alone? Or if non-different, how is the seed not multiple — because of having different essential natures (<s>tādātmya</s>)? Or rather, these two are one, because of having a single essential nature.
