If it is said: 'When earth and the like are to be produced, their material cause is already a different form of the earth-seed and so on' — then the seed is not independent in producing earth and the like. Because if they were independent of it, the emergence of the sprout would be untenable. And it is you yourself who have said that non-contributing factors are not to be relied upon. And since the contribution of a moment is impossible apart from production — because [the moment] is indivisible — therefore multiplicity too does not exist, and thus the second absence of the pervader is also not established. Therefore, [there is] uncommon inconclusiveness (<s>asādhāraṇānaikāntika</s>), like the property of having smell (<s>gandhavattva</s>). If one thinks that even non-contributing factors are cooperative conditions that must be relied upon — because their presence and absence are regulated by the effect, and because they cooperate — [we reply:] Then by this logic, even a non-momentary entity will require non-contributing cooperative conditions that are sequential, whose positive and negative concomitance are reproduced by sequential effects. And [the non-momentary entity] will produce effects sequentially, under the influence of sequential cooperative conditions — thus [there is] failure of the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). [Thus:] Existence (<s>sattva</s>) has doubtful exclusion and is inconclusive in proving momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>).

body.text: atra brūmaḥ / kīdṛśaṃ punarapekṣārthamādāya kṣaṇikesāpekṣānapekṣatvanivṛttirūcyate / kiṃ sahakāriṇamapekṣata iti sahakāriṇāsyopakāraḥ karttavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here we reply: What kind of meaning of 'dependence' (<s>apekṣā</s>) is being taken such that the exclusion of both dependence and independence in the momentary is stated? [Does it mean:] 'It depends upon a cooperative condition (<s>sahakārin</s>)' in the sense that the cooperative condition must render assistance (<s>upakāra</s>) to it?

body.text: atha pūrvvāvasthitasyaiva vījādeḥ sahakāriṇā saha sambhūyakaraṇaṃ / yadvā purvvāvasthitasyetyanapekṣamilitāvasthasya karaṇamātramapekṣārthaḥ / atra prathamapakṣasyāsambhavādanapekṣaiva kṣaṇikasya kathamubhayavyāvṛttiḥ / yadyanapekṣaḥ kṣaṇikaḥ, kimityupasarpaṇapratyayābhāve 'pi na karoti / karotyeva yadi syāt / svayamasambhavī tu kathaṃ karotu / atha tadvā tādṛgvā āsīditi na kaścidviśeṣaḥ / tatastādṛksvabhāvasambhavepyakaraṇaṃ sahakāriṇi nirapekṣatāṃ na kṣamata iti cet / asambadvametat / varṇasaṃsthānasāmyepyakarttustatsvabhāvatāyā virahāt / sa cādyātiśayajanakatvalakṣaṇaḥ svabhāvaviśeṣo na samānāsamānasantānavarttiṣu vījakṣaṇeṣu sarvveṣveva sambhavī kintu keṣucideva karmmakarakara pallavasahacareṣu / nanvekatra kṣetre niṣpattilabanādipūrvvakamānīyaikatra kuśūle kṣiptāni sarvvāṇyeva vījāni sādhāraṇarūpāṇyeva pratīyante, tat kutastyo 'yamekavījasambhavī viśeṣonyeṣāmiti cet /

ucyate / kāraṇaṃ khalu sarvvatra kāryye dvividhaṃ dṛṣṭamadṛṣṭañca sarvvāstikaprasidvametat / tataḥ pratyakṣaparokṣasahakāripratyayasākalyamasarvvavidā pratyakṣato na śakyaṃ pratipattuṃ / tato bhavedapi kāraṇasāmagrīśaktibhedāttādṛśaḥ svabhāvabhedaḥ keṣāñcideva vījakṣaṇānāṃ yena taeva vījakṣaṇā ādyātiśayamaṅkurambā paramparayā janayeyu rnānye vījakṣaṇāḥ / nanu yeṣūpasarpaṇapratyayasahacareṣu svakāraṇaśaktibhedādādyātiśayajanakatvalakṣaṇo viśeṣaḥ sambhāvyate, sa tatrāvaśyamastīti kuto labhyamiti cet / aṅkurotpādādanumitādādyātiśayalakṣaṇāt kāryyāditi brūmaḥ / kāraṇānupalabdhestarhi tadabhāva eva bhaviṣyatīti cet / na dṛśyādṛśyasamudāyasya kāraṇasyādarśanepyabhāvasidveḥ kāraṇānupalabdheḥ sandigdhāsidvatvāt / tadayamarthaḥ / pāṇisparśavataḥ kṣaṇasya na bhedabhinnānyakālakṣaṇādbhedo veti matadvaye mitibalaṃ yasyāstyasau jitvaraḥ / tatraikasya balaṃ nimittavirahaḥ kāryyāṅgamanyasya vā / sāmagrī tu na sarvvathekṣaṇasahā kāryyantu mānānugamamiti //

tadevaṃ nopakāro 'pekṣārtha ityanapekṣyaiva kṣaṇikasya sahakāriṣu nobhayavyāvṛttiḥ / atha sambhūyakaraṇamapekṣārthaḥ / tadā yadi pūrvvasthitasyeti viśeṣaṇāpekṣā tadā kṣaṇikasya naivaṃ kadācidityanapekṣaivākṣīṇā / atha pūrvvāsthitasyetyanapekṣyamilitāvasthitasyaiva karaṇamapekṣārthastadā sāpekṣataiva nānapekṣa / tathā ca nobhayavyāvṛttirityasidvaḥ prathamo vyāpakānupalambhaḥ / tathaikatvānekatvayorapi vyāpakayoḥ kṣaṇikādvyāvṛttirasidvā / tattadyāvṛttibhedamāśrityopādānatvādikālpanikasvabhāvabhede 'pi paramārthata ekenaiva svarūpeṇānekakāryyaniṣpādanādubhayavyāvṛtterabhāvāt / yacca vījasyaikenaiva svabhāvena kārakatve kṣityādīnāmaṅkurasvābhāvyāpattiranyathā kāraṇābhede 'pi kāryyabhede 'pi kāryyasyāhetukatvaprasaṅgādityuktaṃ tadasaṅgataṃ / kāraṇaikatvasya kāryyabhedasya ca paṭunendriyapratyakṣeṇa prasādhanāt / ekakāraṇajanyatvaikatvayorvyāpteḥ pratihatatvāt / prasaṅgasyānupadatvāt / yacca kāraṇābhede kāryyābheda ityuktaṃ tatra sāmagrīsvarūpaṃ kāraṇamabhipretaṃ sāmagrīsajātīyatve na kāryyavijātīyatetyarthaḥ / na punaḥ sāmagrīmadhyagatenaikenānekaṃ kāryyaṃ na karttavyaṃ nāma / ekasmādanekotpatteḥ pratyakṣasidvatvāt / na caivaṃ pratyabhijñānāt kālabhedepyabhedasidvirityuktaprāyam / na cendriyapratyakṣaṃ bhinnadeśaṃ sapratighaṃ dṛśyamarthadvayamekamevopalambhayatīti kvacidupalabdhaṃ yena tatrāpi bhedaśaṅkā syāt / śaṅkāyāmbā paṭupratyakṣasyāpyapalāpe sarvvapramāṇocchedaprasaṅgāt / nāpi sandigdhavyatirekaḥ / kṣityāderdrabyāntarasya vījasvabhāvatvenāsmābhirasvīkṛtatvāt anupakāriṇyapekṣāyāḥ pratyākhyānāt / vyāpakānupalambhasyāsidvatvāyogāt / tadetau dvāvapi vyāpakānupalambhāvasidvau na kṣaṇikāt sattvannivarttata iti nāyamasādhāraṇo hetuḥ / api ca vidyamāno bhāvaḥ sādhyetarayoraniścitānvayavyatireko gandhavattādivadasādhāraṇo yuktaḥ / prakṛtavyāpakānupalambhācca sarvvathārthakriyaivāsatī ubhābhyāmbādibhyāmubhayasmādvinivarttitatvena nirāśrayatvāt / tat kathamasādhāraṇānaikāntikī bhaviṣyatyalaṃ pralāpini nirbbandhena / tadevaṃ śaktasya kṣepāyogāt samarthavyavahāragocaratvaṃ jananena vyāptamiti prasaṅgaviparyyayayoḥ sattve hetorapi nānaikāntikatvamataḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgasidviriti sthitam //
body.translated_text: Thus, since assistance is not what is meant by dependence, even without [such] dependence, there is no exclusion from both [alternatives] for the momentary with respect to cooperative conditions (<s>sahakārin</s>). Now, if acting-together is what is meant by dependence — then if the dependence is qualified [as meaning] 'of that which has persisted from before,' then for the momentary this is never the case, so the non-dependence [argument] remains undiminished. But if, setting aside [the qualification] 'of that which has persisted from before,' the acting of what has [merely] come together is what is meant by dependence — then there is indeed dependence, not non-dependence. And thus, [the claim that] there is no exclusion from both — the first non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalambha</s>) is unestablished. Likewise, the exclusion of oneness and manyness — which are also pervaders — from the momentary is unestablished. Because, even though there is a conventionally constructed difference of nature — such as being a material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) and so forth — based on the different exclusions from those [categories], ultimately, since multiple effects are accomplished by a single own-nature, there is no exclusion from both. And the objection that was stated — that if the seed has causality by one and the same nature, there would be the unwanted consequence that earth and the like would acquire the nature of a sprout; otherwise, even when there is no difference in the cause, the difference in effects [would imply] the causelessness of the effect — that is incoherent. Because the oneness of the cause and the diversity of effects are established by keen sense-perception (<s>paṭu indriya-pratyakṣa</s>). Because the pervasion between being produced by a single cause and being one [in effect] is blocked [by counter-evidence]. Because the absurd consequence does not arise. And as for what was said — 'when there is no difference in cause, there is no difference in effect' — there, the aggregate (<s>sāmagrī</s>) in its own form is the cause intended; the meaning is that when [aggregates] are of the same type, the effects are not of different types. But it does not follow that a single [element] within the aggregate cannot produce multiple effects. Because the arising of many from one is established by perception. Nor can it be said, as was nearly stated, that through recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>) identity is established even across temporal difference. For it has never been observed anywhere that sense-perception apprehends two visible objects occupying different locations and possessing resistance as one single thing — such that there could be a doubt of difference even there. Because if [one entertains] doubt [even there], and keen perception is thereby discredited, there would be the absurd consequence of the destruction of all means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). Nor is there doubtful negative concomitance (<s>sandigdhavyatireka</s>). Because earth and the like, being a different substance, are not accepted by us as having the nature of a seed. Because dependence that contributes nothing has been refuted. Because there is no grounds for the non-apprehension of the pervader to be unestablished. Thus these two non-apprehensions of the pervader are [both] unestablished. Existence (<s>sattva</s>) does not withdraw from the momentary — therefore this is not an uncommon reason (<s>asādhāraṇa hetu</s>). Moreover, an existing entity, having undetermined positive and negative concomitance with respect to the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) and its opposite, would be [properly called] uncommon, like possessing fragrance and the like. But from the non-apprehension of the pervader under discussion, causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyā</s>) would be entirely non-existent, being withdrawn from both [the momentary and the non-momentary] by both [arguments] such as pot and the like — and thus being without any basis. So how could it be an uncommon inconclusiveness? Enough of this insistence by the babbler! Thus, since delay is impossible for what is capable, being within the scope of the conventional usage of capability is pervaded by [actual] production. Therefore, with the reason [of existence] established through both <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) and <s>prasaṅgaviparyaya</s> (reversal of the reductio), there is no inconclusiveness. Hence it is established: momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) is proven.

body.text: iti sādharmyadṛṣṭānte 'nvayarūpavyāptyā
body.translated_text: Thus, through the <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion) in the form of positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) in the homologous example (<s>sādharmyadṛṣṭānta</s>),

body.text: kṣaṇabhaṅgasidviḥ samāptā //
body.translated_text: the <s>Kṣaṇabhaṅgasiddhi</s> (Proof of Momentary Destruction) is complete.

body.text: kṛtiriyaṃ mahāpaṇḍitaratnakīrttipādānāmiti //
body.translated_text: This is the composition of the venerable <s>Mahāpaṇḍita Ratnakīrti</s>.
